findings.claim: Each month 5.7 percent of wages must go into JHT: 2 percent from the worker and 3.7 percent from the employer (Pemerintah Republik Indonesia, 2015b).
findings.evidence: S: The figures are right and so are 'each month' and 'must', but only for the population the cited article covers. The bound key (docs/sources.json pp46_jht_contribution, locator 'JHT contribution for wage earners whose employer is not a state organ') quotes PP 46/2015 Pasal 16(1) (sources/text/pp_46_2015.txt:428-434): 'Iuran JHT bagi Peserta penerima Upah yang bekerja pada Pemberi Kerja selain penyelenggara negara sebesar 5,7% ... 2% ... ditanggung oleh Pekerja; dan ... 3,7% ... ditanggung oleh Pemberi Kerja'. 'Each month' is supported by Pasal 17(1), whose base is 'Upah sebulan' (txt:447), and Pasal 19(2), 'wajib membayar Iuran ... setiap bulan' (txt:512). 'Must go into JHT' is supported by Pasal 19(1), 'wajib menyetor Iuran JHT ... sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 16 kepada BPJS Ketenagakerjaan' (txt:507-509). All three hold only inside Pasal 16's scope, and the sentence drops that scope, so it reads as covering all wages. The scope matters for three reasons. Pasal 3 (txt:131-134) sends JHT at state employers to a separate regulation, so PP 46 sets no rate for those workers. Pasal 2(1) (txt:116-121) phases employer registration in ('sesuai penahapan kepesertaan'). BPJS's IR 2024 (sources/text/bpjs_ir_2024.txt:8426-8437) counts 29,308,491 active wage-earner members in JKK/JKM against 18,425,867 in JHT. Round 1 deleted 'JHT is compulsory for wage earners' on exactly these grounds (r1:item:18). Round 2's fix (r2:extra:L2) turned the descriptive 'goes in' into the normative 'must go into JHT' on 'wages' and did not narrow it, even though the L2 skeptic flagged the Pasal 16 scope and Pasal 3. The sentence now states the deleted universal again, this time with a rate. It is live in the published MDX at line 22. | skeptic S: Re-checked against the stored text. docs/sources.json pp46_jht_contribution has the locator 'Pasal 16 ayat (1): JHT contribution for wage earners whose employer is not a state organ'. Its quote matches sources/text/pp_46_2015.txt:428-434 ('Iuran JHT bagi Peserta penerima Upah yang bekerja pada Pemberi Kerja selain penyelenggara negara sebesar 5,7% ... 2% ... Pekerja ... 3,7% ... Pemberi Kerja'). 'Each month' is supported inside that scope by Pasal 17(1), 'Upah sebulan' (txt:447), and by Pasal 19(2), 'setiap bulan' (txt:512). 'Must' is supported by Pasal 19(1), 'wajib menyetor Iuran JHT ... sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 16' (txt:507-509). All of this holds only inside the Pasal 16 scope: Pasal 3 (txt:131-134) sends JHT at state employers to a separate PP, and Pasal 4(1) (txt:140-143) limits wage-earner Peserta to non-state employers. Pasal 1(3) (txt:66-69) defines Peserta as a person who has paid contributions, and Pasal 2(1) (txt:118-121) phases registration ('sesuai penahapan kepesertaan'). sources/text/bpjs_ir_2024.txt:8427-8437 gives 29,308,491 active PU members in JKK/JKM against 18,425,867 PU in JHT. Round 2's change does fix L2's problems: the sentence now names JHT, and 'must' is an obligation rather than an outcome. But 'wages' has no scope. The bound key, sources.json pp46_jht_contribution, quotes Pasal 16(1): 'Iuran JHT bagi Peserta penerima Upah yang bekerja pada Pemberi Kerja selain penyelenggara negara sebesar 5,7% ... dari Upah'. The section heading at pp_46_2015.txt:420-422 has the same scope. Pasal 3 (pp_46_2015.txt:131-133) moves participants at state employers to a separate Peraturan Pemerintah. Pasal 2(1) (:116-119) obliges employers only 'sesuai penahapan kepesertaan' (by phased membership). Read alone, the sentence makes 5.7 percent compulsory on every Indonesian wage. findings.evidence: H: Excerpt, MDX line 4: 'BPJS has not published the rate it credits to JHT balances for the years after 2020.' Read alone, as on a card: 'the rate it credits ... for the years after 2020' reads as the rate for years 2021 onward. It cannot be read as a length of time, because that would need a quantity ('for five years'), and 'the years after 2020' gives none. The excerpt's own earlier sentence ('From 2005 to 2020, ...') also gives the window. It is true for every year after 2020: 2021 to 2025 are unpublished (evidence under item 2), and the 2026 annual rate is not set until the November accounts (Peraturan BPJS 3/2020 Pasal 2(6) and 4(1), sources/provenance/rules/peraturan_bpjs_3_2020.pdf). A BPJS official might point to Pasal 4(4), which sets the January monthly rate for claims at the December deposit counter rate. That is a formula for claim payouts, not a published rate credited to balances, so it does not refute the sentence. The present tense 'credits' fits: Pasal 5(1) distributes the annual rate every 1 January.
